title: I released an AI-assisted indie game demo on Steam. Here's my experience
author: Zestyclose-Date-8476
selftext:
Late 2023, I started building a game.

I already had a lot of experience with programming and Unity, way before AI, so I knew what I was doing. At least for the most part; the rest I learned during the process, as always.

Since I'm a solo developer, this is a hobby/passion project, and my budget is limited, once AI started appearing as a possibility that could assist me, I embraced it about a year ago.

It mainly helped me with art assets (I can't draw a dot), while I focused on the code and the fun part: game design.

This was around two years after the start of the project. By then, I already had a solid gamplay base

With time, I also started using some Codex to help refine certain aspects and save time.

The whole process went smoothly this past year, and I slowly started promoting the game in different communities and social media.

A few days ago, I released the demo on Steam.

Since the game has a Steam page, I disclosed that I use GenAI for some of the art assets, so now I'm "branded."

Naturally, after releasing the demo, I started promoting the game much more actively here and there, tring to get people to actually play it.

I've had at least one comment on almost every post pointing out that I use AI, as if I had killed someone.

In some communities, the post was even deleted as "low effort" because of the use of AI.

Low effort... after three years.

Besides that, I submitted the game to some festivals and got rejected because of the use of GenAI. I've contacted streamers who replied that they can't show the game because it uses GenAI, and I've had many other similar experiences.

So, you understand where I'm going.

From a marketing perspective, we're treated like evil witches that have to be burned.

Is this a rant? Maybe, in a way.

But it's also an encouraging post, because despite all that, I'm almost at 1k wishlists, which isn't bad. I'm not going to be Balatro, but at least I'm getting somewhere.

Also, BECAUSE AI helped me reach this stage, I'm now hiring an artist to help me with some of the art: capsules, splash screens, UI, and now a lore video.

So I'm pretty sure this artist wouldn't have this work from me if it weren't for AI.

  
That's it. I would like to hear similar experiences and your opinion.

comments.author: keaslenyt
comments.body:
I can fully relate, I spent every free waking minute in the last 6 months working on my game and getting branded as "low effort" or swept under the rug as "AI Slop" just makes my blood boil, but I think I'm now starting to get desensitised to it I guess, I just don't care any more. Every time I make a post - I also get at least a couple Anti-AI warriors who feel it is their duty to voice their opinion. I keep wanting to say - "if there was no AI use, then there would be no game, so you wouldn't play it anyway, so should I care that you won't play my game? You weren't going to anyway" but you got to be civil with these folks...  
  
At the end of the day - every time I post and I get these responses - my steam wishlists grow, in fact you can kinda correlate the number of Anti-AI comments and number of wishlists you get, so I now look at them as a sort of indicator ;)

The important thing is - they will be the first to tell you - if you make a good game then it doesn't matter what it looks like, which I find very funny. If it doesn't matter what it looks like then why have your panties in a knot? Why is it  that an artist can have their own style and I cannot? 

But I think I may have a potential solution for this - I am busy setting up a crowd funding channel (I'm thinking Ko-fi or something like that) so that anybody who wants to put up their money for me to hire human artist can do so. If I hit the target with that, I will hire human artists and I will have all the game art redone and I will implement it and release it as a free add-on/expansion. And then we can see how many of these do-gooders actually give half a damn about the human artists they seem to support so fiercely...

comments.author: khuzait_haircut
comments.body:
The way to win this game is not to play it. Don't contact streamers or post in communities. I learned the latter the hard way. Most of the time it would not have gotten you much attention anyway. Don't take any of this personally. A vast majority of people who play your game won't like it because that's how it goes.

Then you have the AI haters. There's no point in engaging with them. Nothing good will come out of it. In time they will come around because the genie is not going back into the bottle.

I put up a demo of a game I made with a lot of AI assets and I'm at thousands of wishlists and hundreds of playthroughs. Yes, you'll get the "oh no AI!" posts and comments. Read the feedback, what are they really complaining about? If you can fix and keep the vision of your game it then its probably a good idea to fix it.

If I sell a hundred copies next year I'll be satisfied. I really think that's the healthiest approach to this.

Because more often than not, they create something with AI that wouldn’t have ever been possible and there’s issues with the code that create bugs or do malicious things unintentionally.

comments.author: imnotabot303
comments.body:
There's a post like this almost everyday here now, it's almost as tedious as the anti AI comments.

What people need to think about is that there are pros and cons to AI and for a lot of people, the cons are seen as outweighing the pros by quite a large amount.

Nobody cares if one good game/video/image/song is made if they have to dig through hundreds more that are low effort trash. The only way to try and battle that is if AI communities stop being an AI circlejerk and start self regulating the slop, and platforms try and get better curation so that the low effort content sinks to the bottom quickly.

On top of the mountains of slop being produced, the anti AI sentiment has just become a popular bandwagon to jump on. YouTubers with millions of subs are constantly shitting on AI in every form because it gets them views. Then you have hordes of their devoted fans agreeing with them and spreading that further online. Even mainstream news stations have jumped onto the AI apocalypse clickbait bandwagon.

There's people constantly pushing stories about AI using up all the water, going rogue like it's a sci-fi movie, ruining the environment, data centers taking over everywhere, AI creating new viruses, taking everyone's jobs, sending people into an "AI psychosis" and any number of other dystopian scenarios etc. People just hear these stories and repeat them not even caring if they are true or not and to what scale. 

That's not even counting the whole creative side of things.

Unfortunately when something like this becomes popular online lots of people just jump on it for monetary gain whether they believe what they are saying or not. Outrage sells.

This has happened again and again throughout history with almost every technology that shakes up society and industry, many people just can't handle change. On top of that it's now exacerbated to extreme amounts via the internet and social media creating group think.

It's a losing battle that will go away slowly with time but I doubt anytime soon. People just need to deal with the fact that AI is vastly unpopular online right now with a lot of people and you're not going to change their minds with a single good game or any other piece of media.

comments.author: Osirian_Legacy
comments.body:
I think the anti-ai people do have some ground to stand on. The massive water usage and electricity cost to the locals isn’t something to just shrug off, it’s a pretty huge waste and actually impacts real people.

Also, using GenAI for art literally does put an artist out of work. Prior to GenAI you didn’t have the option to not hire an artist or not learn yourself. Sure, that also meant if you didn’t want to learn or hire someone the game just wouldn’t exist. 

Is that okay for things not to exist because of someone’s choices? That’s not for me to answer, that’s more a personal opinion. 

I use AI too, more as a coding assistant but I do still use it so I’m not saying anyone here is a bad person for using it but you cannot say in good faith that people who are against AI don’t have a good reason to have that stance.

replies.author: Osirian_Legacy
replies.body: There’s also another side of this where, if you do use AI there IS a lot of backlash against it. It should be expected and planned for. I’m not entirely sure why folks are still surprised about that.

comments.author: tbconquest84
comments.body: I'd love to be able to release a game without AI art assets but I'm 42 and  work full time with 4 kids, a wife and everything else that goes along with that. I can't afford a commercial grade artist to do all my backgrounds and character art etc..its just not possible and on the other end why pay for some crappy art from the low end of the spectrum that would drag the game down too. If I could I'd release with AI gen art with the goal of removing/replacing it if the game was moderately successful but I'm sure even then you'd get hit with disdain and negative feedback..Like you want stick figures and chicken scratch and shit ass placeholder art, (which I'd barely have time to do that either)?? It's stupid because some people have ideas and vision beyond their own capabilities/time/funding. I've dreamt of making my own games since I was a kid and now AI has taken a huge burden of that off my plate but guess we'll never know. This type of shit is discouraging.

comments.author: gentlemaningreen
comments.body:
Similar story here. The part of this hobby I actually enjoy is game design. I started making games a few years ago and got nowhere, and I have about a dozen unfinished ideas sitting on a drive to prove it.

What changed was embracing AI in my day job as a Product Manager. Once I understood how to work with it, applying the same thing to game development did two things at once: it pushed my own learning further, and it made more intricate games possible for someone with my constraints. Full-time job, three kids, everything else. I don't get to noodle on an idea for five years and still expect to play the finished thing. I'm almost 50 years old and I want to live to play some of my game ideas.... :D

The design is 100% mine. Every decision about how it plays, what it rewards, and what gets cut has been made by me, and most of them were made twice because the first version wasn't fun. Whether the code behind that arrives in 6 to 12 months with AI or in 4 to 5 years without it makes no difference to the player. It makes an enormous difference to whether the player ever gets to see it at all.

I'm not expecting to make money. I'd just like players to finish a session and be able to tell the thing was built with care, because it was. If I did it right, they won't feel it was built with AI, even though it was.

comments.author: dannydek
comments.body: It’s a phase, driven by desperation. Deep down, they know everything is about to change. Soon, anyone will be able to create beautiful games, with today’s limitations fading away. A single person will be capable of building experiences that surpass what entire studios can produce today. The technology is improving month after month. Within a few years, this won’t be the exception. It’ll be the norm.

comments.author: WalkingDadPG
comments.body:
Let’s see what next fest brings. My game is registered for next fest, full AI disclosure on code and assets. 

The world is changing, and AI certainly won’t stop. People are using it in so many areas. I’m a web dev, former game dev (worked for Limbic Entertainment, the guys behind the not so good version of Heroes of Might and Magic). Do people really think these studios wouldn’t use the help of AI if it helps producing quality code and assets? It’s a business after all. But this doesn’t mean the games are all bad AI slop. Maybe we are even getting more BETTER games because people with great ideas are now able to build their games without any need of curators or publishers? 

We use copilot at work for web development. Rarely looking at the code as even Uncle Bob said. It’s about constraints, steering, architecture, the right guardrails and harness in general. 

I just LOVE that I’m now able to build what I have in my mind without spending years. With full-time work and a family i simply don’t have the time to spent years on a single product. But a few months? Failing fast? Thats awesome. 

Anyways, I could go on but don’t want to spend my Saturday morning ranting.

Cheers
